name: WordPress
title: WordPress analytics, cookieless and EU-hosted
description: Add cookieless, EU-hosted analytics to any WordPress site by pasting one snippet into a free header-code plugin. No coding, no theme files, works with any theme or page builder.
tagline: Cookieless analytics for WordPress in about five minutes, no code required.
intro: Privytics is cookieless, EU-hosted analytics for WordPress. You add it by pasting one snippet into a free plugin, so there is no coding and no theme files to touch. It works with any theme or page builder, and your page views start counting the moment you save. The whole thing takes about five minutes.

why.title: No coding, works with any theme
why.body: You paste one snippet into a free plugin. It does not matter whether you use a classic theme, a block theme, or a builder like Elementor or Divi. There is nothing to set up in your theme and no files to edit.

why.title: Cookieless, so a simpler banner story
why.body: Privytics sets no tracking cookies. It counts visitors with a daily-changing anonymous fingerprint instead of a stored id, so there are no analytics cookies to list in a cookie banner. Whether your site still needs a banner depends on your other tools, but Privytics adds none.

why.title: Installs in minutes, removes just as easily
why.body: The whole setup is one snippet in one box, so it takes a few minutes. To undo it, you just delete the snippet. There are no database changes and nothing left behind.

why.title: Running a shop? Track sales too
why.body: If you sell with WooCommerce and want orders and revenue, follow the Privytics WooCommerce guide. It adds sales tracking on top of the page views you set up here.

steps.title: Install a free plugin
steps.body: In your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins, then Add New Plugin. Search for WPCode, then click Install Now and Activate. WPCode is free and lets you add code to your whole site from one box, so you never have to open a theme file. Any header-and-footer code plugin works the same way; these steps use WPCode.
steps.code: Plugins  >  Add New Plugin  >  search "WPCode"  >  Install  >  Activate

steps.title: Paste the snippet and save
steps.body: In the left menu open WPCode, then Header & Footer. Paste the snippet below into the Header box and click Save Changes. You do not need to understand the code, just copy it exactly. The one thing to change is YOUR_CLIENT_ID: replace it with the client id from your Privytics dashboard, keeping the quote marks.
steps.code:
<script>
  window.op=window.op||function(){var n=[];return new Proxy(function(){arguments.length&&n.push([].slice.call(arguments))},{get:function(t,r){return"q"===r?n:function(){n.push([r].concat([].slice.call(arguments)))}} ,has:function(t,r){return"q"===r}}) }();
  window.op('init', {
    apiUrl: 'https://api.privytics.com',
    clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
    trackScreenViews: true,
    trackOutgoingLinks: true,
  });
</script>
<script src="https://privytics.com/op1.js" defer async></script>

steps.title: Check that it is working
steps.body: That is the whole setup. Open your website and click through a page or two, then open your Privytics dashboard and look at the Realtime view: your visits show up within a few seconds, and page views keep counting on their own from now on. One tip: if your site uses a caching plugin, clear its cache once so the snippet is live for every visitor.
steps.code:
Your site  >  click through a few pages
Privytics dashboard  >  Realtime  >  watch your visits appear

faq.q: Do I need a developer or to edit any files?
faq.a: No. Install a free plugin like WPCode, paste the snippet into its Header box, and save. Nothing touches your theme files. If you would rather add it in code, a developer can put the same two tags into a child theme's functions.php using the wp_head hook, but that is optional and most sites do not need it.

faq.q: Does Privytics set cookies or need a cookie banner?
faq.a: Privytics is cookieless. It counts visitors with a daily-changing anonymous fingerprint rather than a stored id, so it sets no tracking cookies and there are none to list in a banner. Whether your site still needs a banner depends on your other tools, but Privytics itself adds none.

faq.q: I pasted the snippet but see no data. What is wrong?
faq.a: The usual cause is caching. If you use a caching plugin such as WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache or LiteSpeed, or a CDN like Cloudflare, clear the cache and reload. Then check that you replaced YOUR_CLIENT_ID with your real client id, and that you pasted the snippet into the Header box (not Footer).

faq.q: Can I track clicks, events, or WooCommerce sales?
faq.a: Page views track automatically. To record a specific action like a signup, call window.op('track', 'signup') from a Custom HTML block on the page where it happens, for example a thank-you page. For shop orders and revenue, follow the Privytics WooCommerce guide. For most sites, the automatic page views are all you need.

sourcesUsed: Local repo: apps/api/src/routes/track.router.ts, apps/api/src/utils/auth.ts (verified ingestion contract), packages/sdks/web/src/init-snippet.ts (verified op stub byte-for-byte), packages/sdks/web/src/index.ts (verified trackScreenViews/trackOutgoingLinks/trackAttributes options), packages/validation/src/track.validation.ts (verified zTrackPayload shape)
omitted: Simplified for clarity after feedback that the first version was hard to understand. Changes: (1) removed op1.js / window.op / 'OpenPanel engine' jargon from the intro; (2) reduced to three no-code steps (install, paste, check) instead of four; (3) dropped the data-track event tutorial from the steps because it required editing the pasted snippet (trackAttributes is not set in it), which confused non-technical readers; (4) moved the functions.php / wp_head code path and custom-event tracking into plain FAQ answers instead of numbered steps.

Custom events: the guide no longer shows the data-track attribute. Verified in packages/sdks/web/src/index.ts that data-track only fires when trackAttributes:true is set, which the pasted snippet deliberately does not set. The events FAQ uses window.op('track', ...) from a Custom HTML block instead, which works with the pasted snippet as-is and fires on page load (accurate for thank-you-page style events, not raw button-click tracking).

The functions.php / wp_head code alternative is real and verified (add_action('wp_head', cb) with static HTML cannot fatal a site) but is now mentioned only in the 'do I need a developer' FAQ, to keep the main flow no-code. The tags it would print are the same two shown in step 2.
window.op stub reproduced byte-for-byte from getInitSnippet() in packages/sdks/web/src/init-snippet.ts (including the '}} ,has:' spacing). Left unchanged.

Hosts: the snippet sets apiUrl to https://api.privytics.com and loads the tracker from https://privytics.com/op1.js. The op1.js file is served by the marketing site itself (apps/public/public/op1.js), so the URL resolves once privytics.com is deployed.

Header-code plugin: step 1 leads with WPCode (WordPress.org slug insert-headers-and-footers) only, to avoid the near-identical-name collision with the separate 'Insert Headers and Footers' plugin. Exact WPCode menu labels (Header & Footer > Header) can shift between versions and were taken from research, not re-verified against a live install this session.
Caching guidance names WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache, LiteSpeed and Cloudflare as common cases; standard operational practice, not re-verified against each product's docs this session.

No PHP SDK and no official Privytics/OpenPanel WordPress plugin exist, so the optional code path uses raw WordPress hooks and step 1 recommends a generic third-party plugin. The copy does not imply any official plugin.

Cookieless wording simplified to 'daily-changing anonymous fingerprint' in the reader-facing copy (the precise mechanism is a daily-rotating salted hash of IP, user agent and project id). Not legal advice; whether a site needs a consent banner depends on its other scripts and jurisdiction.
Plan details (10,000 events/month free, 12-month free / 5-year paid retention, session replay on paid) are left off this install-focused page.
